title: Bryan Cantrill on LLMs and the Peril of Laziness Lost
description: Bryan Cantrill argues that LLMs inherently lack the virtue of laziness - work costs nothing to an LLM, so they don't optimize for future time or develop crisp abstractions. This highlights how essential human laziness is: our finite time forces us to develop good abstractions because we don't want to waste time on clunky ones.
author: Bryan Cantrill (quoted by Simon Willison)

title: Gemma 4 E2B Audio Transcription with MLX
description: Simon shared a recipe for transcribing audio files on macOS using the 10.28GB Gemma 4 E2B model with MLX and mlx-vlm. The command uses uv run with Python 3.13 and the mlx_vlm package to transcribe audio files effectively.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrej Karpathy: Growing Gap in AI Capability Understanding
description: Andrej Karpathy tweeted about the growing gap in understanding of AI capability based on access points and domains. OpenAI's free 'Advanced Voice Mode' runs on older GPT-4o era models and fumbles basic questions, while their highest-tier paid Codex model can coherently restructure entire codebases or find vulnerabilities. This works because coding domains offer explicit reward functions verifiable through unit tests and are more valuable in B2B settings.
author: Andrej Karpathy (covered by Simon Willison)

title: Karpathy's Shift from AI Coding to Second Brain
description: Andrej Karpathy reportedly stopped using AI to write code and is instead focusing on using LLMs to build a 'Second Brain' - a personal knowledge base system. He developed an LLM Knowledge Base architecture that bypasses traditional RAG, using an evolving markdown library maintained by AI with tools like Obsidian for capturing notes and web articles.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Karpathy's 'AI Psychosis' Warning for Developers
description: Andrej Karpathy warned about 'AI psychosis' among developers, saying he 'started to lose his ability to code' due to over-reliance on AI programming tools. He predicted 2026 would be the 'Slopacolypse' and mentioned that 'AI is suddenly writing most of his code' causing him to 'start to atrophy his ability to write code.' By early 2026, 51% of all code committed to GitHub was generated or substantially assisted by AI.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Meta's Muse Spark Model Launch with Interesting Tool Capabilities
description: Meta announced Muse Spark, their first model release since Llama 4 almost exactly a year ago. It's hosted (not open weights) and currently in private API preview, but available on meta.ai with Facebook or Instagram login. The model features interesting tool capabilities and reasoning features.
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic's Project Glasswing - Restricting Claude Mythos to Security Researchers
description: Anthropic didn't release their latest model, Claude Mythos, to the public. Instead, they made it available to a very restricted set of preview partners under Project Glasswing. Simon discusses why this sounds necessary given the security implications of powerful AI models.
author: Simon Willison

title: GLM-5.1: 754B Parameter Model with Advanced Code Generation
description: Chinese AI lab Z.ai's GLM-5.1 is a 754B parameter, 1.51TB MIT-licensed model. Simon tested its ability to generate SVG with CSS animations, including fixing broken animations when pointed out. The model demonstrated sophisticated understanding of SVG, CSS transforms, and animation issues.
author: Simon Willison

title: Google AI Edge Gallery: Local Gemma 4 on iPhone
description: Google released AI Edge Gallery, an official app for running Gemma 4 models (E2B and E4B sizes) directly on iPhone. The 2.54GB E2B model is fast and useful. The app includes image questions, audio transcription (up to 30s), and interesting 'skills' demos showing tool calling against eight different interactive widgets implemented as HTML pages.
author: Simon Willison

title: Eight Years of Wanting, Three Months of Building with AI
description: Lalit Maganti's deep dive into building syntaqlite, high-fidelity devtools for SQLite. The project took 8 years of thinking but only 3 months of building, thanks to AI. Key insights: AI excels at tedious work (400+ grammar rules) but can cause procrastination on design decisions. The first vibe-coded prototype worked as proof of concept but had poor architecture, requiring a complete restart with more human decision-making. AI struggles with tasks that have no objectively checkable answer like design.
author: Lalit Maganti (covered by Simon Willison)
